arizona state won with their defense saturday, opposed to the normal formula of outscoring their opponent – beating oregon state 30-17 and forcing 4 interceptions. the sun devils remain in the drivers’ seat to make the pac-12 title game, but they have to beat ucla on the road this weekend.

baylor jumped up to #3 in the ap poll, but remained #4 in the bcs following their 63-34 win over texas tech. tests still remain for this team, though, with oklahoma state, tcu and texas left on the schedule.

central florida barely beat temple saturday, paying the price in the polls. the scarlet knights still have a strong case for a bcs game, remaining atop the aac, with their only loss coming to south carolina.

clemson played on thursday, easily beating georgia tech 55-31 at home. in true southern football fashion, the tigers play the citadel this weekend… before closing with south carolina on the road, a game that will have bcs implications.
despite the controversy surrounding the noles’ this week, they went out and pounded syracuse 59-3. their acc schedule is officially wrapped up, they close the season with idaho and florida.
fresno state had a bye this weekend, the bulldogs get new mexico at home on saturday.

funny how things can change in a week. oregon, after beating utah 44-21, is once again in the pac-12 north driver seat after a stanford loss. the ducks should be able to navigate through arizona and oregon state – but mariota’s health has to remain a concern. for the 2nd straight week, he totaled negative rushing yards.
how about them duke blue devils! after a 48-30 win over miami, duke now controls their destiny in the acc coastal division. that is not a misprint. they close with wake forrest and north carolina.

it was a close call for the top ranked tide, but they eventually outlasted mississippi state by a final of 20-7. bama is somehow allowed to play chattanooga this weekend, before an iron bowl for the ages – winner goes to the sec title game.

it was a clunker, but south carolina found a way to beat florida 19-14 saturday. the gamecocks still have a chance at the sec title, their conference schedule is done, but they need a missouri loss. spurrior takes on coastal carolina and clemson to close the season.

lsu had the weekend off, and they needed it to prepare defensively to stop texas a&m and johnny manziel. the tigers were one of the few defenses to figure out the heisman winner last year, but a win this year would likely keep manziel from winning the award back-to-back years.
michigan state clinched their spot in the big 10 title game, with a clutch 41-28 win over nebraska in lincoln this weekend. the spartans close with northwestern and minnesota.
missouri had the weekend off, benefiting on the polls because of it. the tigers remain the top team in the sec east, but have to get through ole miss and south carolina to get there.
much like their aac counterpart ucf, louisville barely beat houston 20-13 saturday. not much more to say about this garbage conference.
northern illinois defeated ball state, 48-27 thursday night to remain undefeated.
ohio state improved to 10-0 on the season, with a 60-35 win over illinois. the buckeyes welcome indiana to columbus this weekend, before traveling to ann arbor to close out with michigan
oklahoma bounced back from an embarrassing loss to baylor, pounding iowa state 48-10 in norman. kansas state and oklahoma state remain on the schedule for the sooners.

oklahoma state went through some growing plays in the middle part of the season, but the cowboys are clicking on all cylinders now. they handed mack brown his worst home loss during his tenure at texas, with a 38-13 win. now – a primetime test we’ve been waiting for, vs baylor saturday night.
ole miss found their way back into the dirty poll, with a 51-21 win over troy. strong showing this season, by the team who took home the nation’s #1 recruiting class.

stanford went from pac-12 north front runner, to potentially the alamo bowl with a 20-17 loss saturday night to usc. the game showed if you have the size and strength, stanford is a beatable team. the cardinal close with cal and notre dame.

talk about a turnaround… this usc lost 10-7 to washington state in la, let that sink in. saturday night, the trojans defeated #5 stanford 20-17 on a last second field goal. ed orgeron might not get the sc job next season, but he’ll get a job somewhere else after what he’s done for this program. usc still has an outside shot at the pac-12 title game, they’ll have to beat colorado and ucla to stay alive though.
texas a&m had a bye this weekend, but two huge games remain: at lsu this weekend, then at home versus missouri.
ucla played friday, and beat washington 41-31 in la. the bruins still control their own destiny in the pac-12 south, with two must-watch games remaining – vs arizona state and at usc.

what. a. finish. no doubt, the end to the auburn vs georgia game will be shown on highlight reels for years to come. the implications were huge, as now auburn can win the sec west with an iron bowl win over alabama, in two weeks.
wisconsin continued to play tremendous football, beating indiana 51-3 in madison this weekend. the badgers close with minnesota and penn state.

competitive pressure in european dairy farming is increasing due to progressing liberalisation of the eu milk market. existing agricultural economic methods proved to be insufficient to provide reliable estimates on regional competitiveness and future locational production shifts within europe. the goal of this paper is to develop an explorative approach for questioning dairy farmers. in this way an additional scientific contribution to estimate production shifts shall be provided. the approach was developed within the networks 'european dairy farmers' and 'agri benchmark' and the survey was conducted among european dairy farmers. a nonrepresentative selection of these farms is the basis for this regionally differentiated analysis. plans and expectations of participating farmers provide indications of regional developments in dairy production as well as individual developments in dairy farming and management strategies on the farm level. finally the complete questioning approach is evaluated, and suggestions for future conceptual improvements are made in order to develop a suitable, longterm analytical instrument.

der wettbewerbsdruck in der europäischen milchviehhaltung nimmt durch die fortschreitende liberalisierung des eu-milchmarktes zu. bestehende agrarökonomische forschungsmethoden sind nur begrenzt dazu in der lage, belastbare abschätzungen der regionalen wettbewerbsfähigkeit und künftiger standortverlagerungen innerhalb europas zu treffen. ziel der vorliegenden arbeit ist es, in einem explorativen verfahren einen befragungsansatz zu schaffen, mit dem ein ergänzender beitrag für eine solche vorhersage geleistet werden kann. der befragungsansatz wurde innerhalb der netzwerke 'european dairy farmers' und 'agri benchmark' entwickelt und in europäischen milchviehbetrieben eingesetzt. eine nicht repräsentative auswahl dieser betriebe bildet die grundlage für die vorliegende regional differenzierte analyse. die planungen und erwartungen der befragten landwirte geben sowohl hinweise auf regionale entwicklungen in der milchproduktion als auch auf einzelbetriebliche produktionsentwicklungen und managementstrategien. abschließend wird der befragungsansatz hinsichtlich seiner eignung als nachhaltig nutzbares analyseinstrument beurteilt und es werden vorschläge zur künftigen weiterentwicklung unterbreitet.

after losing a shocker on the road to utah, stanford has now put together back-to-back impressive wins. saturday night, they caught ever break – knocking off oregon state in corvallis 20-12. tickle me disappointed once again; their offense is about as anemic as they come. but they’ll get a chance to prove me wrong a week from thursday – when the #2 ducks come to town.

another close win for the canes, resulted in them being bumped down a spot in the polls. a week after sneaking by north carolina, miami struggled with wake forrest this weekend. no more time to debate the canes’ though – they face florida state on the road this weekend.

another team that saw their dreams go up in flames this weekend – texas tech. after starting 7-0, and being one of the best stories in all of college football, the red raiders fell 38-30 at oklahoma this weekend. they have an immediate shot at redemption, though, when oklahoma state comes to town saturday.
auburn played florida atlantic. seriously. but, they won and moved up in the polls. they’ll get the train wreck that is arkansas this saturday.
central florida debuts in the “dirty poll” after a 62-17 win over winless uconn. after a weekend off, they welcome in 6-1 houston.
hey there, irish! welcome back into the “dirty poll!” a 45-10 win over air force, putting notre dame at 6-2 on the year… check that, make it 7-2 with navy this coming weekend.

johnny manziel had another unreal game, continuing to build his case for a 2nd straight trip to new york – beating vanderbilt 56-24. he’ll put up more video game numbers this weekend, when the aggies face utep.

kudos to the bruins – a week after being embarrassed by stanford, they gave everything they had against #2 oregon (tied 14-14 at the half) before being dismantled in the 2nd half. brett hundley has been a major disappointment, mustering only 64 passing yards against oregon and tossing two picks. the good news? the bruins get colorado at home this weekend.
louisville still playing, so i guess we have to talk about it? they bounced back from a dreadful loss to ucf, beating south florida 34-3. the cardinals play winless uconn a week from friday.
lsu played furman. seriously. they have a bye week this weekend, before traveling to take on #1 alabama in tuscaloosa.

man do i love this team. the offense is atrocious, but the spartans belong in the conversation for best defense in the country. they did it again on saturday, mopping the floor with illinois to the tune of 42-3. there are still doubters – and rightfully so. but michigan state has their shot at a statement win, when arch rival michigan comes to town saturday.
michigan had the weekend off, benefiting from attrition and moving up two spots in the poll. huge game for the wolverines saturday – needing a marquee win, they travel to michigan state saturday.

no one seems to be paying any attention to ohio state, and rightfully so. alabama, oregon and florida state are all playing so well – that they buckeyes are an afterthought. but, since they played, i’ll let you know how it went – osu rolled penn state 63-14. they’re at purdue on saturday.

northern illinois continued to make their argument to be a bcs buster for the second straight year, beating eastern michigan 59-20 saturday. they travel to take on massachusetts saturday (which won’t help their bcs chances).

oklahoma needed a good week, to further put the memories of an ass-whooping by texas in their rearview mirror. they did just that – knocking texas tech from the unbeaten ranks, with a 38-30 win in norman. they get another chance to knock off an undefeated team – a week from thursday against baylor.

oklahoma state played their best game in awhile this weekend, winning in dominant fashion 58-27 at iowa state. the cowboys travel to texas tech this saturday, as the red raiders are coming off their first loss of the season.

poor florida state. they absolutely demolished north carolina state, 49-14 the final, but remained at the #3 spot in the polls. they’ll have a chance to jump up this weekend though – with oregon and alabama off, the seminoles face #6 miami (fl) in tallahassee.

rinse and repeat. hard to not feel bad for missouri, leading 17-0 in the 4th quarter – they were on the brink of locking up a trip to the sec title game, and firmly placing themselves in the national title conversation with three consecutive wins over ranked teams. then, overtime happened. missouri missed a chip shot field goal to tie the game, and their season potentially went up in flames. the tigers look to pick up the pieces this weekend at home, against tennessee.

slow start, strong finish. stop me if you’ve heard that before about an oregon game. they were tied 14-14 at the half with ucla, before blowing things open in the 2nd half for a 42-14 win. oregon now gets a weekend off, before the game we’ve had circled on our calendars since the off-season: at stanford a week from thursday.
the badgers had the weekend off – they travel to face iowa this saturday.

the offense keeps on clicking, and the terrible defenses keep getting checked off the list for baylor. it was 59-14 this weekend at kansas, as baylor improved to 7-0 and took over sole place atop the big 12 standings. we’ll find out if they’re for real a week from thursday when oklahoma comes to town.

the tide rolled again (sorry for the lame joke) this time over tennessee 45-10. this one was a blowout from the get go – alabama led 35-0 at the half. after a few head scratching close wins over inferior opponents, bama has kicked things into high gear. it’s a bye week for the top ranked team, then the game we’ve all been waiting for – versus lsu on november 9th.

this was a game for the ages. trailing 17-0 in the 4th quarter, spurrior went back to connor shaw and the gamecocks fought back, tying things at 17 a piece to force overtime. missouri missed a chip shot field to tie the game – keeping south carolina’s hopes alive to make the sec title game. they face mississippi state this weekend at home.

whew. clemson almost pulled another clemson, needing late game heroics to get past maryland on the road. the tigers are basically irrelevant at this point, needing two florida state losses just to make it to the acc title game. but they’ll look to keep any slim chances they have alive this saturday, at virginia.
whoa. close call for the bulldogs, needing ot to beat san diego state on the road, 35-28. they’re battling with northern illinois to get a bcs invite, as they welcome in nevada saturday.

after a week filled with off the field controversy, florida state was lucky to have idaho on the schedule – a game they won 80-14. the problem; those off field issues aren’t going anywhere. the good news? fsu gets florida this week, a team coming off a loss to georgia southern.

all they do is win, win, win… michigan state won again saturday, beating northwestern 30-6, clinching a spot in the big 10 championship game in the process. the spartans close at home against minnesota this weekend.

arguably the most impressive win of the college football season happened saturday night in stillwater – ok state beat down baylor 49-17. i wasn’t a huge believer in baylor, but it’s hard to knock a performance like that. one more win for the cowboys (over rival oklahoma) and they’re big 12 champs, playing in the fiesta bowl.
central florida continued their push to an automatic bcs bid, with a 41-17 win over rutgers. they face south florida on friday.

clemson was irrelevant this past weekend, like they’ve been since that devastating loss to florida state – beating the citadel 52-6. the tigers play south carolina this weekend, with a bcs berth on the line.
for the second year in a row, lsu remains the only defense that somehow, someway slowed down johnny football. 34-10 was the final, a huge win over texas a&m for les miles.

fresno state hopes they bolstered their bid for a bcs game with a 69-28 win over new mexico. not only are they battling themselves, they’re also battling northern illinois for a higher ranking. the bull dogs are at san jose state friday.

i would like to say johnny manziel can kiss his heisman hopes goodbye, after his 3rd loss of the season, but it appears no one wants to win the award this year. sadly, even with three losses, if manziel can beat missouri this weekend – you have to think he still has a shot.

if i told you before the season, auburn would control their destiny to play in the sec title game and potentially the natty, going into the iron bowl – would you believe me? i know i wouldn’t. but that’s how big the stakes are this saturday, against #1 alabama. a win for the tigers, and they head to atlanta, and possibly la.
jordan lynch is a stud. that is all. northern illinois won again, this time 35-17 at toledo, they play 1-10 western michigan thursday night.

missouri continues to control their own destiny to reach the sec championship game, but they need one more win to get there. the tigers knocked off ole miss, 24-10 in oxford, now they get a pissed off texas a&m and johnny manziel. good luck.
oklahoma won at kansas state 41-31 this saturday, bringing up a huge matchup against oklahoma state this weekend.

poor ucla. the bruins have had a fantastic season in jim mora’s 2nd year, but couldn’t knock off a top notch opponent. after a 38-33 loss to arizona state, all three of ucla’s losses have come to teams ranked 13th or higher in the bcs. they get the trojans this weekend, in the battle for la.
she loves me, she loves me not. notre dame (for the 4th time) squeezes back in the dirty poll after a win over byu saturday. the irish get stanford, on the road, this weekend.

south carolina continued their push to upend missouri in the sec east, but they need a tiger loss this weekend if they want to make a trip to atlanta. the gamecocks beat coastal carolina 70-10, and face instate rival clemson this weekend.

talk about a bounce back, stanford took their usc frustrations out on cal 63-13 saturday. more importantly, the pac-12 north game of “hot potato” finally ended with stanford on top, after oregon fell at arizona. the cardinal face notre dame this weekend, before they play arizona state in the pac-12 title game.

the chips continue to fall, and ohio state is left hoping for a lucky break. oregon went down, then baylor; now a potential jameis winston suspension? the buckeyes have to get through michigan in the big house, then michigan state in the big 10 championship game – but they have to feel good about their chances with all the turmoil surrounding the team ranked one spot ahead of them.

the dream season continues for the dukies, after a 28-21 win over wake forrest – the blue devils area now just one win away from an appearance in the acc title game. the team standing in the way; instate rival north carolina.
usc played colorado, no one watched, and one 47-29. the trojans end the season with ucla at the coliseum, will a win make ed orgeron the next head coach?

well, didn’t see this one coming. oregon was flat out embarrassed, humiliated, punched in the mouth (whatever analogy you want to use) in a 42-16 loss to arizona. for the first time in four years, the ducks will not be playing in a bcs game. hard to let that sink in, if you’re a duck fan. there’s not enough room to give an opinion on that turd sandwich, listen to gamenight this week.

well, it’s all come down to one week for a team shooting at a three-peat. the tide cruised through a bye week (vs chattanooga) and now the iron bowl, versus auburn. alabama’s instate rival had the week off to prepare, and this should be one for the ages. the stakes? winner goes to the sec championship game.

i enjoy living in dorms on campus, and am planning to do so even during my junior year when most students decide to live off-campus. the community that is created through floor meetings with your residence assistant is wonderful and there are many programs that you can go to throughout the year to build a sense of community with other people in your building. most of the dorms are updated and are not terribly messy during the week. however, dorms do get a little messier over the weekend because the cleaning crew will not be in friday night until monday morning. sharing bathrooms and common areas with other residents is not a problem, and i love being able to walk down the hallway to hang out with friends that i have made in the building. all dorms have kitchens and common areas. some dorms have fancy common areas complete with pool tables, ping pong tables, televisions, and couches â?? these areas are where students can come together to hang out. last year, during the superbowl, all of the students came together in the downstairs common room to watch the game and cheer on the teams. it was a great experience! i love living in dorms because it gives you a new perspective that you wouldnâ??t necessarily get to see about college life if you were commuting to school.

keene is great for students who want to pursue a career in teaching, or the fine arts; most students who attend here are majoring in either of these two subjects. thatâ??s not to say that students donâ??t choose other majors and fall in love with the school the same way i did â?? that definitely happens! this college is also for students who may be prone to homesickness and need a feeling of togetherness or community â?? which is exactly what keene provides!

keene state college is a warm and welcoming school that thrives on the sense of community and togetherness that is created from the faculty and students. the school has many wonderful academic programs, clubs, organizations, and state-of-the-art facilities that, together, create a stimulating and exciting atmosphere. there are always activities going on and fun places to hang out, so when you do happen to have a bit of free time, you will never be bored!

on the weekends, there is always something to do. you can go for a walk downtown, get an ice cream at piazzaâ??s, fill up a bag of jar candy at life is sweet, go clothes shopping at synergy, visit bars such as cobblestone, lab nâ?? lager, or go out to eat at any of the nice restaurants that are lined up on main street. the best place for pizza is ramuntoâ??s across from cumberland farms because after midnight on the weekends (starting on thursday) they offer large slices of cheese pizza for $2, pepperoni for $2.50, and the most amazing garlic knots you will ever taste, for only $2! that is a popular hangout for a lot of us, especially late at night â?? but i also love going there during the day and eating in the restaurant! there are sometimes late-night programs you can attend, such as groove boston, which is an amazing â??ragerâ?? dance party that goes on in the mabel brown room in the student center on campus. comedians and carnival set ups come to campus, and there are so many other attractions that happen on campus on specific weekends. there are shuttle services that will pick you up at various places on campus and will take you to stores such as target, jcpenney, or mauriceâ??s that are not in walking distance, and the shuttle drivers will gladly pick you up. there are plenty of well-known restaurants that are not on main street but are still close by when you take the shuttle, and those are: chiliâ??s, olive garden, longhorn steakhouse, and applebeeâ??s. there is also a small movie theater near campus which will show movies as they come out, like any normal movie theater. it isn't fancy, or a huge place, but it is a nice place to go to when you want to go see a movie!

student involvement fairs are an amazing way to scope out the clubs and organizations at keene state to find your niche. there are sports clubs, academic clubs, and community service clubsâ?¦ all of which are incredible and i have heard nothing but great things about. i am involved with the keene state relay for life committee, and it is an absolute joy. you wonâ??t find another college with such dedicated students as you will find at keene; no matter what club or organization you are in, you will feel right at home and make a difference.

students who would like to apply to keene state should know a few things before applying. first, keene can work with you if your high school gpa or test scores are not high; i know of students who attend this school with very high scores, and those who have very low scores have been accepted here too. you should also know that teaching is very popular and is one of this schoolâ??s trademarks â?? however, if you are an education major, you will need to take on a liberal arts major as well as fulfill all of your general education course requirements. this makes for a big work load, but it is rewarding, and worth it. from what i have heard; if you have an education degree such as elementary education, and then add your liberal arts major, such as psychology â?? you will only be recognized as having a degree in education during graduation â?? your liberal arts major will not be included in your degree. just something to think about when youâ??re selecting the school if teaching happens to be your major of choice! lastly, keene has plenty of tutors and help available if you do get accepted and feel as though you are struggling in a course. keene has plenty of resources readily available for you to use â?? so even if test-taking is your weak point â?? there are tutors and professors willing to help!

the difficulty of classes really depends on your academic interests, the professor you select, and which classes you pick. some isp (general education) courses can be extremely easy, or extremely challenging, depending on the professor. i had one professor for an intro to geology: earth systems science course that taught the class as though it was our major and gave us labs to work on without any background information. she hardly taught a thing and only had us work on the labs within our groups during class time. this was very challenging for me. however, another student was in a different section of the course, with a different professor, and she had an easy time â?? the professor was very thorough and taught the class in such a way that made learning fun and interesting. so really, it depends on what you like to study (i personally am not a science person), how you learn (i donâ??t learn through labs without thorough explanation beforehand), and the teaching style of the professor. if i were you, i would look up professors on ratemyprofessor.com to see what other students have said about a professor that you are thinking of taking a course with. this website has saved me a lot of trouble and i have been able to pick professors who teach with visual aids and teaching styles that work best for me as a student.

the food at keene is good, especially during your first semester. there is an array of food items that will be served every single day in the dining commons (dc): pizza, pasta with choices of sauce, cheeseburgers, grilled cheese, quesadillas, stir-fry, a salad bar with rotating vegetable options each day, and a deli. the main course changes every meal and is typically a type of chicken or pork, served with a vegetable, and another side as an option. the dc also has a wonderful spread of desserts during lunch and dinner, and the soft-serve ice cream machine is always open. there are pepsi product soda fountains, milk, and juice options as well. the dc opens at 7am on the week days and will stop letting people into the building at promptly 7:30pm each night. you can stay in the dc and finish eating until 8pm when the staff begins to clean up for the night. during the weekend, the dc opens at 10am and will still close at 7:30pm. i am not a fan of these hours, and as a student who works a lot, and takes many classes, this doesnâ??t always leave room to get to the dining commons. however, there are other food options. you can use your meal plan at hoot n scoot which is a fast-food type of setting that has greasy and unhealthy food options at any time of the day, until 9pm. lloydâ??s and the bean and bagel are places that use flex (an option you can have on your meal plan - $150 to use in these places specifically) or you can pay by debit card and cash. these dining areas have longer hours and make it more convenient for a busy college student to grab food or a snack on the way to class.

we always have pumpkinfest, which is when the whole town of keene and surrounding cities come together and carve pumpkins to be shown off and lit up downtown. the entire block is shut down and people come from all over to walk the streets looking at the pumpkins that keene state students, keene residents, and other have spent time carving. there are so many performers, food vendors, and an incredible sense of community during this weekend at keene. i love everything about it. we also have winterfest which is when the student center is decorated for the holidays; students can make build-a-bears, eat marshmallows and other items in the chocolate fountains, listen to christmas music, and just make memories together. itâ??s a great way to relax before finals week. spring weekend is similar, although it is geared more toward outdoor fun. performers come, (such as a group of dancers from mtvâ??s americaâ??s best dance crew), we had a carnival set up on campus complete with carnival rides, cotton candy, fried dough, the dc serves fair food that everyone loves â?? and everyone eats and spends all of their time outside together. we also have the family-style dinner on appian way where everyone sits at this one long table and eats outside together â?? passing plates and sharing memories.

as an occupational therapy student, i can surely say the academic programs are rigorous, but very worth it. students certainly have to put in time and effort into academics, but if you put in all that you have and try your best then you will earn good standing. we also have many services on campus to assist with academics if a student desires to utilize them. i think we have great academics at keuka, and i can say as a senior that i am feelings prepared to go out into the real world due to my coursework at keuka.

dorm life is what you make of it. i have always had fun and enjoyed my experiences in dorms on campus. physically, the dorms aren't new and super modern, and are kind of small, but they certainly work. i currently live in apartments, which are still considered on campus, which have a ton of space and i love them. the dorms for underclassmen aren't quite as spacious, but are fair.

food and dining is something that keuka has been working on improving, and it has improved, but it is not the best. we only have one dining hall due to the size of the school, and options are sometimes limited. there is a small gluten free section, and a nice salad bar. more variety would be nice to have, but we make do. there's a hot line, a sandwich bar, a cereal bar, a salad bar, and an international line that offers different, more unique foods. the food is fair, but not outstanding by any means.

keuka is an absolutely amazing school that offers ample opportunities to students. keuka is the national leader in experiential learning, as students participate in internships beginning freshman year through their senior year, which is my favorite asset of the school. attending keuka has allowed me to open many doors, and has also helped me to develop my skills in being a professional, a leader, and a well rounded person.

keuka is an expensive private school, however they do offer many options and scholarships for financial aid. also, even though it is expensive, the academic experience you receive there is great, so i think it's worth it. as far as the physical layout and building on campus, i wouldn't say it's 100% worth the money, but keuka is working on updating their dorms, buildings, and athletic complex. definitely compare and contrast prices of different schools, but if there is a program you are really interested in at keuka, especially one like occupational therapy, which offers a five year master's program, i would say it's worth the money.
keuka is great for people who love a small, tight knit community feel, and who are interested in hands on experience right from the beginning.
great for these types of students
keuka offers a variety of sports, as well as a great intramural program. i play lacrosse on campus and love it. we have a great reputation at keuka in our conference, which is the neac conference.

the first tip i would give to students exploring keuka would be to really look into the field period program! this is a wonderful experiential learning program we offer at the college, in which students complete an internship every year of their college experience. it is a wonderful program and opens many doors for students. i would also recommend to explore your area of interest, as we have many great programs and wonderful staff. the college is small, so students would have to be sure that would be a good fit for them, but it is a beautiful campus right on a lake and is a wonderful place to be. i would recommend a visit and a meeting with an academic adviser to get started

to be honest, keuka is very rural and not right in a town, so there are no shops or restaurants within walking distance of the campus. however, town is only three miles away, and there are places to go there. on campus, clubs offer a variety of activities, such as movies, dances, holiday activities, and so on for fun. our campus is directly on keuka lake, which is fun. during warmer months, lots of people go swimming or kayaking on the lake. there are also sports and intramural programs. lots of times students just make their own fun since it's a small campus with not a lot around, so it's what you make of it!
we have a trustworthy campus security office at keuka. someone is always on duty, and we also have blue emergency lights in case of emergency.
we have our very own chapel on campus, which offers services for all types of cultures and religions, which is very nice. having the lake right off campus is awesome.

arizona state won with their defense saturday, opposed to the normal formula of outscoring their opponent – beating oregon state 30-17 and forcing 4 interceptions. the sun devils remain in the drivers’ seat to make the pac-12 title game, but they have to beat ucla on the road this weekend.

baylor jumped up to #3 in the ap poll, but remained #4 in the bcs following their 63-34 win over texas tech. tests still remain for this team, though, with oklahoma state, tcu and texas left on the schedule.

central florida barely beat temple saturday, paying the price in the polls. the scarlet knights still have a strong case for a bcs game, remaining atop the aac, with their only loss coming to south carolina.

clemson played on thursday, easily beating georgia tech 55-31 at home. in true southern football fashion, the tigers play the citadel this weekend… before closing with south carolina on the road, a game that will have bcs implications.
despite the controversy surrounding the noles’ this week, they went out and pounded syracuse 59-3. their acc schedule is officially wrapped up, they close the season with idaho and florida.
fresno state had a bye this weekend, the bulldogs get new mexico at home on saturday.

funny how things can change in a week. oregon, after beating utah 44-21, is once again in the pac-12 north driver seat after a stanford loss. the ducks should be able to navigate through arizona and oregon state – but mariota’s health has to remain a concern. for the 2nd straight week, he totaled negative rushing yards.
how about them duke blue devils! after a 48-30 win over miami, duke now controls their destiny in the acc coastal division. that is not a misprint. they close with wake forrest and north carolina.

it was a close call for the top ranked tide, but they eventually outlasted mississippi state by a final of 20-7. bama is somehow allowed to play chattanooga this weekend, before an iron bowl for the ages – winner goes to the sec title game.

it was a clunker, but south carolina found a way to beat florida 19-14 saturday. the gamecocks still have a chance at the sec title, their conference schedule is done, but they need a missouri loss. spurrior takes on coastal carolina and clemson to close the season.

lsu had the weekend off, and they needed it to prepare defensively to stop texas a&m and johnny manziel. the tigers were one of the few defenses to figure out the heisman winner last year, but a win this year would likely keep manziel from winning the award back-to-back years.
michigan state clinched their spot in the big 10 title game, with a clutch 41-28 win over nebraska in lincoln this weekend. the spartans close with northwestern and minnesota.
missouri had the weekend off, benefiting on the polls because of it. the tigers remain the top team in the sec east, but have to get through ole miss and south carolina to get there.
much like their aac counterpart ucf, louisville barely beat houston 20-13 saturday. not much more to say about this garbage conference.
northern illinois defeated ball state, 48-27 thursday night to remain undefeated.
ohio state improved to 10-0 on the season, with a 60-35 win over illinois. the buckeyes welcome indiana to columbus this weekend, before traveling to ann arbor to close out with michigan
oklahoma bounced back from an embarrassing loss to baylor, pounding iowa state 48-10 in norman. kansas state and oklahoma state remain on the schedule for the sooners.

oklahoma state went through some growing plays in the middle part of the season, but the cowboys are clicking on all cylinders now. they handed mack brown his worst home loss during his tenure at texas, with a 38-13 win. now – a primetime test we’ve been waiting for, vs baylor saturday night.
ole miss found their way back into the dirty poll, with a 51-21 win over troy. strong showing this season, by the team who took home the nation’s #1 recruiting class.

stanford went from pac-12 north front runner, to potentially the alamo bowl with a 20-17 loss saturday night to usc. the game showed if you have the size and strength, stanford is a beatable team. the cardinal close with cal and notre dame.

talk about a turnaround… this usc lost 10-7 to washington state in la, let that sink in. saturday night, the trojans defeated #5 stanford 20-17 on a last second field goal. ed orgeron might not get the sc job next season, but he’ll get a job somewhere else after what he’s done for this program. usc still has an outside shot at the pac-12 title game, they’ll have to beat colorado and ucla to stay alive though.
texas a&m had a bye this weekend, but two huge games remain: at lsu this weekend, then at home versus missouri.
ucla played friday, and beat washington 41-31 in la. the bruins still control their own destiny in the pac-12 south, with two must-watch games remaining – vs arizona state and at usc.

what. a. finish. no doubt, the end to the auburn vs georgia game will be shown on highlight reels for years to come. the implications were huge, as now auburn can win the sec west with an iron bowl win over alabama, in two weeks.
wisconsin continued to play tremendous football, beating indiana 51-3 in madison this weekend. the badgers close with minnesota and penn state.

citrus college is a smaller community college, making it slightly easier to get classes, but not that easy because everything is impacted anyway. many of the on campus resources are beneficial, while others seem to waste your time rather than help you. there are a handful of professors who will truly dedicate their lives to teaching you the subjects they are passionate about, which is great.

for students looking for a smaller campus in the area, this is a small one. it is not tiny, but it isn't as big as surrounding schools. it is also very good for students pursuing stem majors because they have a very good stem program.
great for these types of students

it honestly depends on what you are studying, what teachers you get, what they teach, and how often you are on campus. if you are going full time, you will probably notice that you are working a lot, studying a lot, etc. if you are only going for a class or two, it is a much different experience. the general education courses are usually less involved than the major-focused science classes, but many professors are very good. when the teachers care about their subject, they care about teaching it to their students a lot more. i have had better experiences with the higher-level courses.

the biggest tip that comes to mind is not education-related. it is parking-related. you need to show up very early, maybe even an hour early, to get parking here. also, get everything you need done for admission, financial aid, etc. done before the semester begins. once the semester begins, lines in the student services building are too long.

the food on campus is pretty all right. the cafe on campus makes good food. there is also a starbucks on campus and several vending machines. the amount of food around this area is a little much, but you can find anything you want within walking distance. if you have a gap in your class schedule, it's nice to be able to walk less than a half of a mile to some good, inexpensive food.

the school tries to be very good about campus safety. they send out emails/phone call alerts for anything suspicious that happens on or near the campus. they also make sure all students have the campus security phone number in their cell phones, in case of an emergency.
there are many performances put on by the drama and music department. the area is also surrounded with gyms and parks. it is a good area to be a college student in.
there are no dorms at citrus college. however, there are many surrounding apartment complexes that look really nice and safe.
they have a club rush every semester, where they have a variety of different clubs for different types of people. there is an lgbt club, an anime club, cheerleading, and a few others.

this is a community college, so it is less expensive than a four-year university, obviously. however, the book store does not seem to be as inexpensive, but textbooks are textbooks. they are always expensive.

after losing a shocker on the road to utah, stanford has now put together back-to-back impressive wins. saturday night, they caught ever break – knocking off oregon state in corvallis 20-12. tickle me disappointed once again; their offense is about as anemic as they come. but they’ll get a chance to prove me wrong a week from thursday – when the #2 ducks come to town.

another close win for the canes, resulted in them being bumped down a spot in the polls. a week after sneaking by north carolina, miami struggled with wake forrest this weekend. no more time to debate the canes’ though – they face florida state on the road this weekend.

another team that saw their dreams go up in flames this weekend – texas tech. after starting 7-0, and being one of the best stories in all of college football, the red raiders fell 38-30 at oklahoma this weekend. they have an immediate shot at redemption, though, when oklahoma state comes to town saturday.
auburn played florida atlantic. seriously. but, they won and moved up in the polls. they’ll get the train wreck that is arkansas this saturday.
central florida debuts in the “dirty poll” after a 62-17 win over winless uconn. after a weekend off, they welcome in 6-1 houston.
hey there, irish! welcome back into the “dirty poll!” a 45-10 win over air force, putting notre dame at 6-2 on the year… check that, make it 7-2 with navy this coming weekend.

johnny manziel had another unreal game, continuing to build his case for a 2nd straight trip to new york – beating vanderbilt 56-24. he’ll put up more video game numbers this weekend, when the aggies face utep.

kudos to the bruins – a week after being embarrassed by stanford, they gave everything they had against #2 oregon (tied 14-14 at the half) before being dismantled in the 2nd half. brett hundley has been a major disappointment, mustering only 64 passing yards against oregon and tossing two picks. the good news? the bruins get colorado at home this weekend.
louisville still playing, so i guess we have to talk about it? they bounced back from a dreadful loss to ucf, beating south florida 34-3. the cardinals play winless uconn a week from friday.
lsu played furman. seriously. they have a bye week this weekend, before traveling to take on #1 alabama in tuscaloosa.

man do i love this team. the offense is atrocious, but the spartans belong in the conversation for best defense in the country. they did it again on saturday, mopping the floor with illinois to the tune of 42-3. there are still doubters – and rightfully so. but michigan state has their shot at a statement win, when arch rival michigan comes to town saturday.
michigan had the weekend off, benefiting from attrition and moving up two spots in the poll. huge game for the wolverines saturday – needing a marquee win, they travel to michigan state saturday.

no one seems to be paying any attention to ohio state, and rightfully so. alabama, oregon and florida state are all playing so well – that they buckeyes are an afterthought. but, since they played, i’ll let you know how it went – osu rolled penn state 63-14. they’re at purdue on saturday.

northern illinois continued to make their argument to be a bcs buster for the second straight year, beating eastern michigan 59-20 saturday. they travel to take on massachusetts saturday (which won’t help their bcs chances).

oklahoma needed a good week, to further put the memories of an ass-whooping by texas in their rearview mirror. they did just that – knocking texas tech from the unbeaten ranks, with a 38-30 win in norman. they get another chance to knock off an undefeated team – a week from thursday against baylor.

oklahoma state played their best game in awhile this weekend, winning in dominant fashion 58-27 at iowa state. the cowboys travel to texas tech this saturday, as the red raiders are coming off their first loss of the season.

poor florida state. they absolutely demolished north carolina state, 49-14 the final, but remained at the #3 spot in the polls. they’ll have a chance to jump up this weekend though – with oregon and alabama off, the seminoles face #6 miami (fl) in tallahassee.

rinse and repeat. hard to not feel bad for missouri, leading 17-0 in the 4th quarter – they were on the brink of locking up a trip to the sec title game, and firmly placing themselves in the national title conversation with three consecutive wins over ranked teams. then, overtime happened. missouri missed a chip shot field goal to tie the game, and their season potentially went up in flames. the tigers look to pick up the pieces this weekend at home, against tennessee.

slow start, strong finish. stop me if you’ve heard that before about an oregon game. they were tied 14-14 at the half with ucla, before blowing things open in the 2nd half for a 42-14 win. oregon now gets a weekend off, before the game we’ve had circled on our calendars since the off-season: at stanford a week from thursday.
the badgers had the weekend off – they travel to face iowa this saturday.

the offense keeps on clicking, and the terrible defenses keep getting checked off the list for baylor. it was 59-14 this weekend at kansas, as baylor improved to 7-0 and took over sole place atop the big 12 standings. we’ll find out if they’re for real a week from thursday when oklahoma comes to town.

the tide rolled again (sorry for the lame joke) this time over tennessee 45-10. this one was a blowout from the get go – alabama led 35-0 at the half. after a few head scratching close wins over inferior opponents, bama has kicked things into high gear. it’s a bye week for the top ranked team, then the game we’ve all been waiting for – versus lsu on november 9th.

this was a game for the ages. trailing 17-0 in the 4th quarter, spurrior went back to connor shaw and the gamecocks fought back, tying things at 17 a piece to force overtime. missouri missed a chip shot field to tie the game – keeping south carolina’s hopes alive to make the sec title game. they face mississippi state this weekend at home.

whew. clemson almost pulled another clemson, needing late game heroics to get past maryland on the road. the tigers are basically irrelevant at this point, needing two florida state losses just to make it to the acc title game. but they’ll look to keep any slim chances they have alive this saturday, at virginia.
whoa. close call for the bulldogs, needing ot to beat san diego state on the road, 35-28. they’re battling with northern illinois to get a bcs invite, as they welcome in nevada saturday.

if you are looking for something fun to do, the bonnie has lots of things to do. the game room has pool tables, ping pong and a bowling alley. usually on the weekends a fairly new movie is shown in the auditorium which is free for students. ru-space does activities like tie dye shirts and make your own pillow. also there are several clubs that you can participate in that do activities.
if you don't have a job, things like ramen noodles and bottled water are popular. books are expensive so take care of them so they can be resold if you need to.

it is required to live in a dorm your first year. living in a dorm gives you a chance to branch out and meet new people. it also teaches how to live on your own. if you do not know your roommate, you get to experience living and coping with another person. sometimes some people can be obnoxious but overall dorm life is great.
never go out by yourself. always take someone with you because you never now what can happen. it is recommended to travel in groups to be safe.
radford university has a beautiful campus. the professors are nice and very helpful. it is a great college to attend and has lots of interesting programs.

study all that you can. try not to be drawn into the party scenes too often and focus on your studies. there are several places to study and some that are open 24 hours. go to your classes. skipping may seem like a good idea at the time but it hurts you in the long run. don't wait to the last minute to complete work; professors are not as lenient as high school teachers were.

the campus has several different places for you to chose to eat at. the bonnie has starbucks, chik fil a, pinkberry, wild greens and austin grill. dalton has wendy's, abp(sandwich and soup place), a sushi bar, papa john's and the dalton dining center. all the places serve good food.

there are so many different clubs that students can attend. i am in the wildlife society which is where we learn about how to protect animals and take trips like to the zoo and claytor lake where we rescued clams that had washed up. if you are interested in sports but just want to do it for fun, not be on a team, then there are club sports.
turn your work in on time. don't wait until the night before to do papers or assignments. procrastination can get to you but try not to let it take over.
